features.label: Boards (whiteboarding; not in the weighted numbers)

upcoming: .fig import's tail: fixes from real files, connector labels, table cells, filled areas with their own fills (the best-effort import, editable vector networks, the other layer kinds and variable prototype actions landed 2026-10-11): 5–10 h; then checking the rest of the experimental .fig export (landed 2026-10-12; written files open and draw in other software) on effects, images, prototypes and real files: 5–15 h.
Real-file corpus and measured fidelity: 15–30 h.
Tool-by-tool interaction pass against Figma: 40–60 h.

Languages: native reviews of the es (with es-419), fr, de, pt-BR, ja, ko, zh-Hans, id and cs drafts (people), the entries added since each catalog was written, then Hindi, Vietnamese and Arabic (localization-parity).

Multiplayer (M9): accounts and teams on top of the live sessions and the standalone server (transport, hosting, invite links that open the app, document sync, presence with remote text carets, cursor chat and spotlight, per-user undo, reconnect with offline edits, collision-free ids for styles, variables and comments, the browser client, figcraft-server with persistence and share links to edit or view, team libraries on the server landed): 42–84 h.

progress.text: · Non-ASCII layer names transliterate in code export (M6, #1235): classname runs the name through deunicode before its ASCII filter, so 로그인 화면 → rogeuin-hwamyeon, кнопка → knopka, über → uber in the HTML/CSS/React/Leptos class names, component roots and data- variant attributes (SwiftUI/Compose type names unchanged); a name left with nothing (symbols only) takes the node's kind (.text, .frame) instead of layer-, and the 40-character cut lands on a word boundary. New dependency: deunicode (pure Rust tables, zero deps, BSD-3-Clause, the slug crate's base). htmlcodegentests. Numbers unchanged.

· egui 0.37 capture lifecycle: screenshots with hidden or unknown visibility queue, request a hidden paint, and expire after 60 seconds if no capture arrives (headless-tested contract). Logic-only edits, saves and inspection continue while hidden. Native visible GUI and forced hidden-window paint, browser and Wayland behavior remain unqualified; parity percentages are unchanged.

· Open, Save and the folder dialogs start in the folder of the last file or folder picked in the run (#1290): the Linux portal does not remember it between dialogs as the macOS and Windows panels do. A folder deleted since falls back to the system's choice. No numbers change.

· Boards (M12): board pages get a dot grid under their layers (drawn by the canvas render after the page colour, thinned out when zoomed out); a selected connector shows its ends as handles, and dragging one onto another object re-attaches it there, onto empty canvas leaves it free (board.reattach, one undo step, also over MCP); connectors can be curved, and elbows go around the objects they join when the short way would cross them. Checked in the app, through MCP and in the web build (boards-parity).

· Installed weights of an embedded font family (M7, #1246): release builds embed some families with only a few styles (Poppins Regular, Italic and Bold), and the first font scan dropped every installed face of such a family, so an installed Poppins SemiBold or Medium was never offered (a rescan did offer them). The first scan now keeps the embedded faces, which still win for the styles they cover, and offers the installed styles they lack beside them. Regression test in the font database tests. Numbers unchanged.

· Dev Mode tail (M6, gap 16): Measurements kept on the canvas (gap 16): devMode.addMeasurement {from?, to?, side?} places one between two layers, along one side of a layer or (neither) to the layer around it, stored on the layer it starts from (saved in .figcraft, synced, undoable; old files open without them); Dev Mode draws them as labelled redlines that follow the layers, the Inspect tab lists them (those of the selected layer, or every one on the page), places and removes them; devMode.removeMeasurement and devMode.measurements remove and list them; a copy keeps those to layers copied with it. The layers panel is read-only in Dev Mode: rows select and expand, but don't rename, reorder, hide or lock. Dev Mode 98% / 78%.

· Board facilitation (M12): a timer everyone on a board sees (presets or any minutes, pause, resume, a minute more, stop; synced as its end time, so nothing ticks over the network) and voting sessions (votes per person, on everything, on sticky notes or on the selection; a click votes, your badge takes it back; your votes show while it runs, everyone's with a ranked list once it ends; clear results), in a pill at the top right of the board. board.timer, board.timerState, board.vote, board.voteResults; ballots sync per voter. Checked in the app, with two app instances in one live session through a local figcraft-server, and through MCP; the web build compiles (boards-parity).

· Board templates and tables (M12): a templates picker in the board toolbar places a retrospective, a brainstorm, a weekly planner, a flow chart or a kanban board (board.template, all FigCraft's own) as ordinary board objects in one undo step; board.table makes a table of auto layout frames (up to 50 × 20) whose rows grow with their text, edited by row and column from the bar over the selection or board.tableEdit, typed into with a double-click. Boards ~35% → ~40% breadth, 30–60 h → 26–54 h; the weighted numbers are unchanged.
· Plugin widgets take text input and a property menu (M11, gap 6, plugin API 4; older plugins run

· Boards (M12): File ▸ New board makes a board, a file kind of its own saved in .figcraft and carried to people joining a live session. Sticky notes (8 colours, text that shrinks as the note grows, the author's name, Shift+Cmd/Ctrl+Enter for the next one), shapes with text (7 outlines), connectors that re-route when what they join moves (computed in the engine's normalize pass, so local edits, undo and others' edits agree), marker, highlighter and eraser, stamps with the placer's name on hover; a board toolbar, a contextual bar over the selection and the Design panel hidden until asked for; prototyping and Dev Mode refuse on boards. Design files and boards have their own marks (a pen nib, a note) on tabs, the home screen and the Open files list. Checked in the app, with two app instances in one live session, and through MCP; the web build compiles (boards-parity).

· CJK line breaking completes JIS X 4051's kinsoku (M4): the line-start set now also has the halfwidth small kana ｧ–ｯ and small tsu, the halfwidth (semi-)voiced sound marks ﾞﾟ, the spacing (semi-)voiced sound marks ゛゜, the kana iteration marks 〱–〵 and the halfwidth closing parenthesis ｠; the line-end set has the halfwidth opening parenthesis ｟. Text layers, auto layout and the canvas otherwise wrap Japanese as before: ideographs break anywhere and the behaviour suite pins every category plus that a manual newline may still start a line with a prohibited character. Numbers unchanged.

· fill and stroke props accept "none" and null (M1, #1036): node.create, node.set and the other prop appliers map them to an empty fills/strokes list, as fills: [] already did, so an outline-only shape is one call (agents write "none" for no paint; the empty-list form was undocumented). The parameter docs (KEYS, shown by listcommands and the CLI) and docs/mcp.md say so, and the error message names the accepted forms. fillnonetests covers create, set, undo, text and the error. Numbers unchanged.
· CLI option terminator (M0.9): -- ends option parsing, so dash-prefixed

· Control channel while the window is minimised (M8, #720): a minimised or covered window answers every request that acts on the app's state (edits, ui.inspect, ui.pointer, ui.key, ui.type, ui.set, app.quit…) without drawing, and what needs a drawn frame (ui.screenshot, ui.input, window.new) is an error at once; before, those waited up to 60 s and held up every later request on the connection (an attached agent's inspectui or window screenshot stalled until the window came back). Measured on Windows 11, minimised: requests ~100 ms each (eframe wakes a minimised window at most ten times a second; ~2 ms on screen), a window screenshot fails in ~100 ms instead of 60 s, idle CPU 0. Numbers unchanged.

· Number variables on text content (M3, #629): the Typography section's variable picker also lists number variables for a text layer's content, as the engine already accepted (the text shows the number, e.g. 42.5, and follows the variable). Other text fields keep their own types. Numbers unchanged.

· Frames and sections convert into each other (M1, #719): object.convertToSection turns a frame on the page or in a section into a section in place (same box, name, fill and layers, which stay where they are; what only a frame has goes: auto layout, clipping, layout grids, guides, scrolling), and object.convertToFrame now also turns a section into a frame that keeps its fill and doesn't clip, so the look stays. Nested frames, instances, main components and sections holding sections are refused with the reason; one undo step each. Both are in the canvas context menu (Convert to section / Convert to frame) and in Spanish. Numbers unchanged.

· Adobe Fonts found on macOS (M7, #298): fonts activated through Adobe Fonts rendered in the fallback font without a warning, because Creative Cloud keeps them in its own folder as hidden files named by number, which the font scan never read. The macOS scan now includes ~/Library/Application Support/Adobe/CoreSync/plugins/livetype, and files without an extension are indexed when they start with a font signature. Fonts are read in place. Regression test in the font database tests; docs/cli.md lists the folder. Numbers unchanged.

· Auto-save (M1, #305): Preferences ▸ Save files automatically (pref.autoSave, off by default, desktop only) saves each open file that has a path 3 s after its last change, never during a gesture, a live text preview or while a version is shown; the file is encoded off the UI thread, a failed save says why and is tried again a minute later. Numbers unchanged.
· A text box by dragging (M1, #363): a drag with the Text tool makes a fixed-size text box the size of the drag; a click still makes auto-width text. Numbers unchanged.
· Batch step references (M0.9, #400): a command.batch step can use the id an earlier step made ({"$step": n}, a reserved key), so a nested tree takes one call and one undo step. Numbers unchanged.

· Removing someone from a live session (M9, #338): the host or the file's owner removes a person from the avatar's menu or with collab.removePerson; they keep their copy and can't rejoin while the session runs. Numbers unchanged.

· Languages (M10, #257, #263, #469, #477, #288): Russian (one/few/many plurals) and Turkish catalogs reviewed by native speakers, Czech and Indonesian drafts, the Japanese draft completed; Preferences ▸ Language lists 12 languages and Latin American Spanish. Numbers unchanged.
· Zoom previews (M8, #312): when renders from scratch are slow, a new zoom shows the whole view coarsely first, then refines it. Numbers unchanged.
· Web clipboard (M1, #375): copy and paste in the browser go through the system clipboard. Numbers unchanged.
· Alt-drag copies snap to their original and Duplicate (Cmd+D) repeats the last copy's offset (M1, #283). Numbers unchanged.

· Dev Mode tail (M6, gap 16): generated layer trees start with the import lines of the connected components they call, once each per language; Compare changes takes any saved version as the before; a behaviour suite made the Dev Mode canvas inspect-only (no moving, resizing, drawing or editing; menus and shortcuts refuse design edits with a note), added Changed to the ready list and refused statuses on layers inside frames; read-only plugins show their panels from the Inspect tab. Dev Mode 97% / 76%.

· Corner handles win over the corner-radius handles (M1, #292): a press on the inner half of a corner handle's square picked the radius handle 10 px in, so the drag neither resized nor (dragging outward) rounded anything. Inside the drawn square the corner now resizes both sides (in ratio with Shift or the link); further in the radius handle still answers. Regression test in the transform behaviour suite. Numbers unchanged.

· Home screen recent files as cards (M7): each card shows the picture its file carries on its first page's colour, the file's icon, name and "Edited ... ago"; sort by name, creation or last change either way; a table view; a click selects, a double-click or Enter opens, arrow keys move; Open, Show in folder and Remove from recents on right-click. Numbers unchanged.

· SVG/PDF export depth (M0.9, #208): visible descendants deeper than 256 levels below an exported root are refused before bounds or drawing, including masks and raster fallbacks. SVG has a checked API; the engine and CLI report the limit and suggest selecting an inner layer. Existing destination files survive refusal. Boundary, inner-root, hidden-subtree, multi-root/page and command/CLI regressions cover the change. Numbers unchanged.

· Vector edit mode regions (M4): with the Move tool, the filled area under the pointer is hatched with "/" lines in the selection colour, clipped by the area's own fill rule so holes stay clear; the hatch goes near points (3.5 px) and segments (2 px), and its spacing follows octave folding (8 px at every power-of-two zoom), fixed to the shape. A click selects the area with its points (they move with it but keep the unselected look), Shift adds or removes one, a press on a selected area drags the whole selection as one undo step, and a click on an empty spot clears the areas and stays in edit mode. vector.edit.select {regions} and vector.edit.state (regions, regionVertices, regionHover); vectorregionstests and regionstests. Numbers unchanged.

· MCP/control transport hardening (#201): 32 MiB incoming frames are bounded while reading; oversized frames return an error and close without draining. The opt-in loopback control listener caps active workers at 8, applies 60 s socket read/write inactivity timeouts and caps both request queues at 8, discarding timed-out requests including those deferred to hidden windows. Reader, queue, idle-client and blocked-writer regressions cover the limits. Numbers unchanged.

· Attached MCP (M0.9, #194): a transport failure no longer replays a request that may already have edited the document. The caller gets an outcome-unknown error and must inspect before retrying; the next explicit call reconnects. Loopback tests cover a lost mutation reply, a single applied edit, reconnect and a connection failure before sending. Numbers unchanged.

· Constrain proportions in the Layout panel (M1, #220): with the W/H link on, typing a width or height scales the other side by the layer's own ratio; the property edit dropped the ratio, so the link only worked while dragging resize handles. Both sides in one edit stay as typed, the w/h aliases work the same, each layer of a multi-selection keeps its own ratio, and a zero side has no ratio to keep. Regression test in the transform behaviour suite. Numbers unchanged.

· Repeat last command (M1, #181): repeated edits keep the underlying command and parameters, so repeated nudges accumulate with one undo step each. A stored self-reference is refused instead of recursing. Regression tests cover three repeats, their undo steps, and missing or self-referencing commands. Numbers unchanged.

· Component playground (M3): with an instance, a component or a component set selected, the Inspect tab shows a Playground: a preview of the component and a control for each variant, boolean and text property. What is tried there changes the preview and the code in the Code section, never the file (no undo step, the canvas instance stays as it is); Reset goes back to the component's or the instance's own values. component.playground {id?, properties?, language?, path?} gives the same to scripts: the properties with their values, the code, and a PNG on request (playgroundtests). Left: instance-swap and slot properties in the playground (the command takes an instance swap; the panel has no control for it), a code connect template's snippet with the tried values. Numbers unchanged.

· Auto layout, on-canvas handles of automatic gaps (M2): the handle between spread rows or columns (and between items with an auto gap) shows the distance the layout gives the gap instead of the stored value, and dragging it makes the gap a fixed one from there, as typing a gap in the panel does; one undo step (gaphandletests). Before, the drag changed a value that had no effect. The documentation is silent on dragging an automatic gap. Numbers unchanged.

· Variables inside styles (M3): a shared style can bind variables to fields of its value (style.bind {style, field, variable?}: a paint style's colours and gradient stops, an effect style's colour, radius, spread and offsets, a grid style's size, count, gutter and offset, a text style's font size, line height, letter spacing, family and style). Every layer using the style shows those fields resolved in its own modes and stays linked when a variable or a mode changes; the style keeps them resolved in the default modes. A style made from a layer keeps that layer's bindings; a new value drops bindings to what is gone. The style editor binds from its property rows (paint colour, shadow colour, blur radius, grid size) and detaches from the variable's chip; the style picker marks styles that use variables. .fig export and import carry the bindings on the style, REST layers hand theirs to the style they use. Left: binding text style fields and the other effect and grid fields from the editor (commands only), library variables in the picker, a style's library copy. Numbers unchanged.

· Effects on groups, inner shadows and background blur (M3): a group is no outline of its own, so its inner shadows are cast inwards from around what its layers draw together (their pixels, over them: no shade at a seam between two layers) and its background blur and glass show the backdrop through the outlines of its layers (under them). Canvas and PNG; SVG embeds a group with an inner shadow as a render and its background blur as an image under the layers; PDF places both as images, the blur matching the PNG. Where the group holds one shape the pixels match that shape, or a frame filled like it, carrying the effect (groupeffectstests in render, svg and pdf). Offsets and spreads of a group's inner shadow go by whole pixels. Numbers unchanged.

· Text made by commands on a dark page (M1): in the app, text.create and node.create {type: text} that name no fill give white text on a dark page, by the same rule as the Text tool (the page's colour decides, also inside a frame); a named fill, fills or fillStyle is kept. Sessions without an interface (CLI, MCP, exports) still make black text everywhere. Numbers unchanged.

· Frames and groups, a one-step convert (M1): object.convertToGroup and object.convertToFrame (the Design panel's type menu on a frame or a group) change the layer in place, its layers staying where they are on the page. A frame turned into a group loses what only a frame has (auto layout, with the positions it gave kept and fill children fixed; fills, strokes, corner radius, clipping, layout grids, guides, scrolling) and takes its layers' box; a group turned into a frame keeps its box, with no fill and no clipping. Instances, main components, layers inside instances and empty frames are refused with the reason, all or nothing; one undo step. Numbers unchanged.
